problems.objective: Illustrate, calculate, and compare left, right, and midpoint Riemann sums for functions.
problems.fullText:
Complete the following steps for the given function, interval, and value of $n$.

$$f(x)=3x^{2}+2\quad\text{on }[1,3];\quad n=4$$

a. Sketch the graph of the function on the given interval.

b. Calculate $\Delta x$ and the grid points $x_{0},x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}$.

c. Illustrate the left and right Riemann sums, and determine which underestimates and which overestimates the area under the curve.

d. Calculate the left and right Riemann sums.

problems.objective: Evaluate definite integrals using properties of definite integrals.
problems.fullText:
Suppose

$$\int_{3}^{5}f(x)\,dx=4,\qquad\int_{5}^{8}f(x)\,dx=-7,\qquad\int_{5}^{8}g(x)\,dx=1.$$

Evaluate:

a. $\displaystyle\int_{3}^{5}7f(x)\,dx$

b. $\displaystyle\int_{5}^{8}-2g(x)\,dx$

c. $\displaystyle\int_{5}^{8}\bigl[5f(x)-g(x)\bigr]\,dx$

d. $\displaystyle\int_{8}^{5}\bigl[f(x)+3g(x)\bigr]\,dx$

parts.label: Problem
parts.text:

d. $\displaystyle\int_{8}^{5}\bigl[f(x)+3g(x)\bigr]\,dx$

problems.objective: Evaluate definite integrals using properties of definite integrals.
problems.fullText:
Consider two functions $f$ and $g$ on $[2,8]$ such that

$$\int_{2}^{8}f(x)\,dx=15,\quad\int_{2}^{8}g(x)\,dx=6,\quad\int_{4}^{8}f(x)\,dx=7,\quad\int_{2}^{4}g(x)\,dx=4.$$

Evaluate:

a. $\displaystyle\int_{2}^{4}9f(x)\,dx$

b. $\displaystyle\int_{2}^{8}\bigl(f(x)-g(x)\bigr)\,dx$

c. $\displaystyle\int_{2}^{4}\bigl(f(x)-g(x)\bigr)\,dx$

d. $\displaystyle\int_{4}^{8}\bigl(g(x)-f(x)\bigr)\,dx$

e. $\displaystyle\int_{4}^{8}5g(x)\,dx$

f. $\displaystyle\int_{4}^{2}6f(x)\,dx$

parts.label: Problem
parts.text:

$$\int_{2}^{8}f(x)\,dx=15,\quad\int_{2}^{8}g(x)\,dx=6,\quad\int_{4}^{8}f(x)\,dx=7,\quad\int_{2}^{4}g(x)\,dx=4.$$

Evaluate:

a. $\displaystyle\int_{2}^{4}9f(x)\,dx$

b. $\displaystyle\int_{2}^{8}\bigl(f(x)-g(x)\bigr)\,dx$

c. $\displaystyle\int_{2}^{4}\bigl(f(x)-g(x)\bigr)\,dx$

d. $\displaystyle\int_{4}^{8}\bigl(g(x)-f(x)\bigr)\,dx$

e. $\displaystyle\int_{4}^{8}5g(x)\,dx$

f. $\displaystyle\int_{4}^{2}6f(x)\,dx$
